title: CORRECT: write-before-ioctl pattern for KEY_IMPORT; do not embed key bytes in ioctl struct
description: KEY_IMPORT uses write(2) to deliver raw key bytes to the fd's inbuf, then the ioctl struct carries only metadata (algo, provider, keylen, exportable). Why it is right: embedding key bytes in the ioctl struct would require a struct large enough for the worst-case key (ML-DSA-87 at 4896 bytes, CRYPTO2DEV_KEY_IMPORT_MAXLEN=8192 with headroom). That allocation hits the kernel stack on every KEY_IMPORT call — including tiny EC key imports — and violates the ~1KB stack frame guideline. The write-before-ioctl pattern heap-allocates exactly what the key requires and zeroes on completion. What a reviewer might suggest: 'use a __user pointer in the ioctl struct to avoid the two-step.' That would require __user pointer handling, compat32 tracking, and a fixed-size maximum-case allocation. The current pattern is simpler and safer.
close_reason: Audit finding: correct behavior, no action needed
